client.name: NATIONAL MILK PRODUCERS FEDERATION
client.general_description: Develop and carries out policies that advance the well-being of dairy producers and co-ops

lobbying_activities.description: Supported efforts to swiftly and effectively implement the dairy provisions of the 2018 Farm Bill, including the Dairy Margin Coverage program and expanded access to the Livestock Gross Margin program. Child Nutrition - NMPF is monitoring and educating Congress on the effects of child nutrition legislation and programs for dairy farmers, cooperatives, and consumers. NMPF supports efforts to increase kids' access to dairy through nutrition programs. This includes reinstating 1% flavored milk in school breakfast and lunch programs, including as part of the Fiscal Year 2022 Agriculture-FDA Appropriations Act (H.R. 4356, S. 2599), the Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act (H.R. 1861), the School Milk Nutrition Act (H.R. 4635), and the forthcoming FNS rule on school meal standards for the 2024-25 school year and beyond. Supported efforts to increase funding for SNAP and other nutrition programs as well as USDA's flexibility in implementing these programs to support food insecure households during the downturn caused by and the ongoing recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic. Supported the GIVE MILK Act (H.R. 818) to increase milk consumption under the WIC program. Supported legislative and administrative efforts to improve and modify dairy policy, including providing relief to dairy farmers for uncompensated COVID-19-related losses. COVID-19 - Supported the continued implementation of agricultural provisions of the 2020 COVID relief packages [CARES Act (H.R. 748), Families First Coronavirus Response Act (H.R. 6201), HEROES Act (H.R. 6800), and Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (H.R. 133) as signed into law on December 27, 2020] as well as the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (H.R. 1319) to provide relief to farmers and families from the COVID-19 pandemic. Also supported related administrative actions, including Coronavirus Food Assistance Program payments, product purchases, milk disposal compensation, and milk donation assistance. Supported efforts to ensure agricultural producers have access to the capital required to continue operating during and recover from a disaster, including the Paycheck Protection Clarification for Producers Act (H.R. 1246). Supported the Feed Emergency Enhancement During Disasters Act (H.R. 1240, S. 359) to provide farmers with additional flexibility relating to prevented planting requirements due to shortages in feed, as well as related administrative actions. Supported the Broadband for Rural America Act (H.R. 3369), which increases funding for and streamlines broadband development programs, including bringing programs together under the single roof of USDA. Supported the Broadband Internet Connections for Rural America Act (H.R. 4374). Supported the 2020 WHIP+ Reauthorization Act (H.R. 267) as passed by the House Agriculture Committee. Measure reauthorizes the WHIP-Milk Loss program and makes dairy cooperatives eligible to make payments to producers. Supported similar provisions of the Extending Government Funding and Delivering Emergency Assistance Act (H.R. 5305).

lobbying_activities.description: Food, Animal Residue Avoidance Databank (FARAD) - Supported funding for this system to provide the industry with information on how to avoid drug, pesticide, and environmental contaminant residue problems. Mandatory Animal ID - Supported steps to make this mandatory. Preservation of Antibiotics for Medical Treatment - Opposed legislation to avoid "overuse or misuse" of antibiotics in medicine and agriculture due to inappropriate limitations on needed antibiotics. Nonambulatory cattle - Monitored efforts to address animal handling, especially nonambulatory cattle regulations and procedures. Antibiotic Residue - Monitored and provided information relating to efforts to expand the scope of testing for antibiotic residues in animal tissues and milk. Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) Vaccine - Support steps to modernize North America FMD vaccine bank to support vaccine use strategies in the event of a U.S. outbreak. Animal Rights Mandates - Opposed efforts to enact animal rights mandates via federal legislation. Raw Milk Sales - Opposed efforts facilitating the sale of raw milk.

Advocated for Fiscal Year 2022 funding of 2018 Farm Bill programs, including the Farm and Ranch Stress Assistance Network, the Dairy Business Innovation program, conservation programs, broadband, and food aid. Advocated for report language to direct that certain feed additives be classified as foods rather than drugs and supportive of language which urges FDA to enforce standards of identity for dairy products, with related funding. Supported related provisions in the Fiscal Year 2022 Agriculture-FDA Appropriations Act (H.R. 4356, S. 2599, H.R. 2471). In the Senate's Fiscal Year 2022 Labor, Health and Human Services, Education and Related Agencies bill, advocated for the continued inclusion of language to limit OSHA enforcement on farms with fewer than ten employees and continued inclusion of language that prohibits federal funds from being available to agricultural labor unions. In budget reconciliation process, advocated against changes being made to the timing or assessment basis for taxing capital gains on inherited assets (a.k.a. opposed changes to the "stepped-up basis"). Also supported the inclusion of climate smart ag provisions in budget reconciliation, including those included in the Build Back Better Act (H.R. 5376).
EPA Clean Water Rule - Supported efforts to finalize an effective, science-based rulemaking under the Clean Water Act.

Anaerobic Digestion - Supported efforts at USDA to ensure existing Farm Bill energy programs provide adequate opportunities for the development of anaerobic digestion systems on dairy farms. Supported the REAP Improvement Act (H.R.4162), a bill aimed at expanding flexibilities in and access to USDA's Rural Energy for American Program (REAP) while providing additional investments to help more farmers take advantage of the program. Supported RFS Electricity Pathway to make biogas eligible as a renewable fuel.

Immigration Reform - Worked on efforts to reform immigration rules relating to agricultural workers. NMPF supports legislation to ensure that farmers can keep their existing workforce while also creating an effective mechanism to allow them to access new workers. NMPF has worked on legislation including the Dairy H-2A Eligibility Act (H.R. 1571) and the Farm Workforce Modernization Act (H.R. 1603).

Labeling - Ensured food labeling is based on sound science. Milk Standard of Identity - Supported efforts to require FDA to enforce the standard of identity for milk, including supporting the DAIRY PRIDE Act (H.R. 2828 & S. 1346) and provisions in the Fiscal Year 2022 Agriculture-FDA Appropriations Act (H.R. 4356, S. 2599) urging FDA to enforce standards of identity for dairy products. Food Safety - Monitored implementation of the Food Safety Modernization Act. Raw Milk Sales - Opposed efforts facilitating the sale of raw milk.

Estate tax - Supported efforts to reform and repeal estate taxes (H.R. 1712, S. 617). NMPF has also supported legislation that will create and improve tax credits for investment in technology that turns organic matter into biogas energy and removes nutrient particles from manure, including the Agriculture Environmental Stewardship Act (H.R. 3939, S. 2461) which was incorporated into the Clean Energy for America Act (S. 2118). Supported efforts to ensure that farmers can continue to use cash accounting. Supported efforts to ensure that cooperatives could count non-patronage income in the calculation of the 199A deduction as implemented by the Treasury Department. Supported efforts to prevent the elimination of stepped-up basis and delay until sale taxation for capital gains on inhereted assets.

Supported efforts to provide relief for dairy farmers and milk haulers from hours of service rules, including the HAULS Act (H.R. 2486, S. 792). Advocated for changes in federal truck weight limits provided that carriers install sixth-axle safety technology. Supported the DRIVE Safe Act (H.R. 1745, S. 659) to address the ongoing driver shortage facing many industries. Supported the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (H.R. 3684) to reauthorize highway programs. Supported the Ocean Shipping Reform Act (H.R. 4996, S. 3580) to reduce congestion and disruption at ports.

Provided information related to the following issues: Opposed misuse of Geographical Indications by European Union to impede trade and supported robust US tools to combat misuse of IP regulations in ways that restrict generic terms Advocated on the need to pursue new trade agreements and enforce existing ones Impacts on dairy industry of trading partner retaliation, current and potential Advocated for legislative and administration solutions to alleviate ports congestion hindering U.S. dairy exports Advocated on various bilateral trade issues impacting US dairy exports through regulations/policies in foreign markets

client.general_description: Develop and carries out policies that advance the well-being of dairy producers and co-ops

lobbying_activities.description: Supported efforts to swiftly and effectively implement the dairy provisions of the 2018 Farm Bill, including the Dairy Margin Coverage program and expanded access to the Livestock Gross Margin program. Child Nutrition - NMPF is monitoring and educating Congress on the effects of child nutrition legislation and programs for dairy farmers, cooperatives, and consumers. NMPF supports efforts to increase kids' access to dairy through nutrition programs. This includes reinstating 1% flavored milk in school breakfast and lunch programs, including as part of the Fiscal Year 2022 Agriculture-FDA Appropriations Act (H.R. 4356, S. 2599), the Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act (H.R. 1861), the School Milk Nutrition Act (H.R. 4635), and the forthcoming FNS rule on school meal standards for the 2024-25 school year and beyond. Supported efforts to increase funding for SNAP and other nutrition programs as well as USDA's flexibility in implementing these programs to support food insecure households during the downturn caused by and the ongoing recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic. Supported the GIVE MILK Act (H.R. 818) to increase milk consumption under the WIC program. Urged White House to prioritize increasing food access and protecting choice at its White House Conference on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health. Supported legislative and administrative efforts to improve and modify dairy policy, including providing relief to dairy farmers for uncompensated COVID-19-related losses. COVID-19 - Supported the continued implementation of agricultural provisions of the 2020 COVID relief packages [CARES Act (H.R. 748), Families First Coronavirus Response Act (H.R. 6201), HEROES Act (H.R. 6800), and Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (H.R. 133) as signed into law on December 27, 2020] as well as the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 (H.R. 1319) to provide relief to farmers and families from the COVID-19 pandemic. Also supported related administrative actions, including Coronavirus Food Assistance Program payments, product purchases, milk disposal compensation, and milk donation assistance. Supported efforts to ensure agricultural producers have access to the capital required to continue operating during and recover from a disaster, including the Paycheck Protection Clarification for Producers Act (H.R. 1246). Supported the Feed Emergency Enhancement During Disasters Act (H.R. 1240, S. 359) to provide farmers with additional flexibility relating to prevented planting requirements due to shortages in feed, as well as related administrative actions. Supported the Broadband for Rural America Act (H.R. 3369), which increases funding for and streamlines broadband development programs, including bringing programs together under the single roof of USDA. Supported the Broadband Internet Connections for Rural America Act (H.R. 4374). Supported the 2020 WHIP+ Reauthorization Act (H.R. 267) as passed by the House Agriculture Committee. Measure reauthorizes the WHIP-Milk Loss program and makes dairy cooperatives eligible to make payments to producers. Supported similar provisions of the Extending Government Funding and Delivering Emergency Assistance Act (H.R. 5305).

lobbying_activities.description: Food, Animal Residue Avoidance Databank (FARAD) - Supported funding for this system to provide the industry with information on how to avoid drug, pesticide, and environmental contaminant residue problems. Mandatory Animal ID - Supported steps to make this mandatory. Preservation of Antibiotics for Medical Treatment - Opposed legislation to avoid "overuse or misuse" of antibiotics in medicine and agriculture due to inappropriate limitations on needed antibiotics. Nonambulatory cattle - Monitored efforts to address animal handling, especially nonambulatory cattle regulations and procedures. Antibiotic Residue - Monitored and provided information relating to efforts to expand the scope of testing for antibiotic residues in animal tissues and milk. Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) Vaccine - Support steps to modernize North America FMD vaccine bank to support vaccine use strategies in the event of a U.S. outbreak. Animal Rights Mandates - Opposed efforts to enact animal rights mandates via federal legislation. Raw Milk Sales - Opposed efforts facilitating the sale of raw milk.

Advocated for Fiscal Year 2023 funding of 2018 Farm Bill programs, including the Farm and Ranch Stress Assistance Network, the Dairy Business Innovation program, conservation programs, broadband, and food aid. Advocated for report language to direct that certain feed additives be classified as foods rather than drugs and supportive of language which continues the allowance of 1% flavored milk in school feeding programs and maintains amounts for dairy options in WIC food allowance packages. Advocated for plus up funds for the COVID relief PMVAP program to be used to address the gap in reimbursement for farmers affected by the program's 5 million pound cap. Supported related provisions in the Fiscal Year 2023 Agriculture-FDA Appropriations Act (H.R. 8239). In budget reconciliation process, advocated against changes being made to the timing or assessment basis for taxing capital gains on inherited assets (a.k.a. opposed changes to the "stepped-up basis"). Also supported the inclusion of climate smart ag provisions in budget reconciliation, including those included in the Build Back Better Act (H.R. 5376).
EPA Clean Water Rule - Supported efforts to finalize an effective, science-based rulemaking under the Clean Water Act.

Anaerobic Digestion - Supported efforts at USDA to ensure existing Farm Bill energy programs provide adequate opportunities for the development of anaerobic digestion systems on dairy farms. Supported the REAP Improvement Act (H.R.4162), a bill aimed at expanding flexibilities in and access to USDA's Rural Energy for American Program (REAP) while providing additional investments to help more farmers take advantage of the program. Supported RFS Electricity Pathway to make biogas eligible as a renewable fuel.

Supported efforts to ensure that farmers can continue to use cash accounting. Supported efforts to ensure that cooperatives could count non-patronage income in the calculation of the 199A deduction as implemented by the Treasury Department. Supported efforts to prevent the elimination of stepped-up basis and delay until sale taxation for capital gains on inhereted assets.

Supported efforts to provide relief for dairy farmers and milk haulers from hours of service rules, including the HAULS Act (H.R. 2486, S. 792). Advocated for changes in federal truck weight limits provided that carriers install sixth-axle safety technology. Supported the DRIVE Safe Act (H.R. 1745, S. 659) to address the ongoing driver shortage facing many industries. Supported the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (H.R. 3684) to reauthorize highway programs. Supported the Ocean Shipping Reform Act (H.R. 4996, S. 3580) to reduce congestion and disruption at ports.
